title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 58 (Refusal of Registration and Appeal Against Refusal)

content.overview: Section 58 provides that if a private company limited by shares refuses to register a transfer or transmission of shares, it must send notice of refusal to the transferor and transferee (or person giving intimation of transmission) within thirty days of the date on which the instrument or intimation was delivered. Public companies generally may not refuse registration of transfer of securities. Aggrieved persons may appeal to the Tribunal within the prescribed period; the Tribunal may direct registration or confirm refusal and give consequential directions.
content.glance: Private company: notice of refusal within 30 days; public company: generally no refusal of transfer; appeal to Tribunal; Tribunal may direct registration or confirm refusal.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 58 (Refusal of registration and appeal against refusal). If a private company refuses to register a transfer or transmission, it must send notice of refusal within 30 days of delivery of the instrument or intimation. The transferor, transferee or person giving intimation may appeal within 30 days of receiving the refusal notice, or within 60 days from delivery of the instrument/intimation if no notice is sent. A public company generally must not refuse registration of transfer; where it does so without sufficient cause, the transferee may appeal within 60 days of refusal, or within 90 days from delivery of the instrument/intimation if no intimation of refusal is received. The Tribunal may direct registration or confirm refusal and give consequential directions, including damages where authorised. Contravention of a Tribunal order is subject to the penalty stated in subsection (6). Apply the current text and any applicable exceptions to the facts.

sections.heading: Private company refusal notice
sections.body: A private company that refuses transfer or transmission must send notice of refusal within 30 days from delivery of the instrument of transfer or intimation of transmission.

sections.heading: Appeal against private company refusal
sections.body: The transferor, transferee or person giving intimation may appeal within 30 days of receipt of the refusal notice, or within 60 days from delivery of the instrument/intimation if no notice is sent.

sections.heading: Public company refusal and appeal
sections.body: A public company generally must not refuse registration of transfer. If it refuses without sufficient cause, the transferee may appeal within 60 days of refusal, or within 90 days from delivery of the instrument/intimation where no intimation of refusal is received.

sections.heading: Tribunal powers
sections.body: The Tribunal may direct registration of the transfer/transmission or confirm refusal and give incidental or consequential directions, including damages where authorised by the section.

sections.heading: Contravention of Tribunal order
sections.body: Subsection (6) provides a criminal penalty for contravention of an order under section 58. Verify the current statutory wording and penalty before applying it to a particular proceeding.

provisions.title: Refusal of registration and appeal against refusal

examples.title: Private company refusal notice
examples.body: A private company refuses a transfer under its articles and sends notice within thirty days. The transferee may appeal to the Tribunal under s. 58.

examples.title: Public company refusal
examples.body: A public company refuses to register a duly completed transfer without statutory ground. Section 58’s general bar on public company refusal is engaged; the aggrieved party may appeal.

hypotheticals.question: A private company sends a refusal notice 20 days after delivery of the transfer instrument. By when may the transferee appeal?
hypotheticals.analysis: The appeal period is 30 days from receipt of the refusal notice. If no notice had been sent, the alternative period is 60 days from delivery of the instrument or intimation.

hypotheticals.question: A public company refuses transfer and gives no intimation of refusal. What appeal period should be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 58(4) provides an appeal period of 90 days from delivery of the instrument or intimation where no intimation of refusal is received.

distinctions.title: Refusal appeal and rectification
distinctions.left: Section 58 challenges refusal to register transfer/transmission and provides appeal timelines.
distinctions.right: Section 59 addresses wrongful entry/omission, default/delay and other rectification grounds.

rows.right: Apply section 59 and procedural rules to the case

misconceptions.trap: Using the same appeal period for private and public company refusals.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the separate timelines in subsections (3) and (4), including the no-notice/no-intimation alternatives.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a private company's articles make refusal immune from Tribunal review.
misconceptions.correction: A refusal remains subject to the statutory notice and appeal framework.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the public-company non-refusal rule as eliminating all statutory exceptions.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the current section text and any applicable statutory exception to the transaction.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the key appeal periods under section 58?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Private company: 30 days from refusal notice, or 60 days from delivery if no notice. Public company: 60 days from refusal, or 90 days from delivery if no intimation of refusal.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What can the Tribunal order?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It may direct registration of the transfer/transmission or confirm refusal and give incidental/consequential directions, including damages where authorised.
